# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your coaches first, not members.** Sit down with each coach individually (30 mins max) and ask: "What do you actually deliver?" Get specifics—circuit classes, 1-on-1 strength coaching, nutrition guidance, mobility work. Let them define their own offer. This prevents you building a menu that doesn't match reality on the gym floor.

• **Price by outcome, not time.** Don't list "Personal Training - £50/hour." Instead: "6-Week Strength Build (2x weekly, 1-on-1) - £360" or "Drop-In Classes - £12 per session." Members buy results, not duration. Coaches will know what transformation costs them.

• **Create TWO menus simultaneously:** One internal (for coaches showing what's available to sell to members) and one for your website/marketing (what members see). The coach version should include margins, caps, and any upsells. The member version is clean, benefit-focused, no pricing confusion.

• **Build it in a Google Sheet first, not a designer.** Real data beats pretty. Share the draft with 3-4 loyal members and 2 coaches this week. Ask: "Would you buy this? What's missing? What's confusing?" Iterate based on real feedback, then design once you know it works.

• **Bundle ruthlessly.** Don't sell individual services. Create 3-4 tiers (e.g., "The Starter," "The Athlete," "The Transformation") that include class access + coaching + some add-on. Bundles reduce decision paralysis and increase average member value immediately.
